ev.q: VE against COVID-19 hospitalization was 82% (95% CI = 77%–86%) for 2 doses and 97% (95% CI = 95%–99%) for 3 doses
Among 1,385 case-patients, 931 (67%), 408 (29%), and 46 (3%) had received 0, 2, and 3 mRNA vaccine doses
receipt of a third dose increased vaccine effectiveness against hospitalization among adults without and with immunocompromising conditions
Separate models were generated for immunocompetent adults and adults with immunocompromising conditions.
Control patients were hospitalized with or without COVID-19–like illness and received negative SARS-CoV-2 test results by NAAT.

methods_quotes.q: VE against COVID-19–associated hospitalization was estimated using logistic regression, comparing the odds of being vaccinated versus being unvaccinated
The regression model included case-patient or control status as the outcome variable and an indicator variable for vaccination group
Separate models were generated for immunocompetent adults and adults with immunocompromising conditions.
post hoc comparisons were performed with the pwcompare function in Stata
Control patients were hospitalized with or without COVID-19–like illness and received negative SARS-CoV-2 test results by NAAT.
VE was calculated separately comparing 2-dose recipients to unvaccinated controls and 3-dose recipients to unvaccinated controls.
